clue.text: Record keeping has caught sight of built-up area

indicators.note: keeping means the record word holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: to record is to tape

C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone recording a cityscape, the camera capturing a view of a built-up area.
explanation.definitionFit: A townscape is a view or picture of an urban scene, a sight of a town.

clue.text: Beat poet's last hour on outside broadcast

indicators.note: last tells us to take only the final letter of poet

explanation.surface: A Beat poet's final hour on a radio broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat' looks like the Beat poets; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A throb is a pulse or rhythmic beat.

parts.note: an insinuation is a sly suggestion

clue.text: Outrageous form of execution?

definitions.meaning: electric shock, as in the electric chair, is a way of putting someone to death

explanation.definitionFit: Shocking means appalling; jokingly, giving a shock is how an electric chair kills.

clue.text: After less than a month, beds trees

parts.note: April is a month
cots are beds

explanation.walkthrough: 'less than' removes a month's final letter; 'After' sets the beds word behind it.

clue.text: Termination's accepted by secretary to produce growth

explanation.walkthrough: 'by' gives X as in 'two by four' dimensions.

clue.text: Blue, black and white colouring almost coats area

parts.note: B is the pencil abbreviation for black

parts.note: dye is a colouring

explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' looks like one of the colours listed; it is the definition, meaning risqué.

clue.text: Briefly expressed disapproval about private dance

briefly means the expressed disapproval word is cut short by its last letter

a GI is an American private soldier

explanation.surface: Someone tutting briefly at an intimate dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'private' is an American soldier, not a secret.

clue.text: Playful wag, he re-released a Burton film

explanation.definitionFit: Richard Burton starred in this 1968 Second World War action film.

clue.text: Cultivation of rye, steady in the past

indicators.note: cultivation means the letters of rye steady are worked over into a new order

clue.text: Bitterness controlled French heart but not English

parts.note: coeur is French for heart

explanation.walkthrough: 'but not' removes E from COEUR, leaving COUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancour is deep-seated resentment, a synonym of bitterness.

clue.text: Claim about stopping journalists

parts.note: the press is journalists collectively

clue.text: Initiation of broadband connection produces viewing interruption

explanation.surface: Starting up a broadband connection causes the picture to drop out.
explanation.definitionFit: A blink is a momentary closing of the eyes, interrupting what one sees.

clue.text: What shows ten-pieced moving (or a lot more)?

definitions.text: What shows ten-pieced moving (or a lot more)?

indicators.note: moving means the letters of ten-pieced are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: A riddle about something on ten legs or many more.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: the creature shows (ten) pieces moving, i.e. legs, or a lot more than ten.
explanation.definitionFit: Its name means a hundred feet, though it may have far fewer or more, so many legs in motion describe it.

clue.text: In-house work getting around newspaper computer department's conflict

clue.text: Happy with loss of illumination?

explanation.definitionFit: Delighted means very pleased; split as de-lighted it jokingly means having had its lights removed.

clue.text: Stick with pale daughter

parts.note: wan means pale

explanation.surface: A walking stick belonging to a sickly daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: A wand is a thin rod, a kind of stick.

clue.text: 60 Minutes covering North Dakota because it's an American state

parts.note: sixty minutes make an hour

as can mean because

explanation.definitionFit: Honduras is a sovereign country of Central America, a state in the Americas.

clue.text: Unconventional, including fine Greek letters, frequently shortened

shortened means the frequently word loses its last letter

parts.note: often means frequently

explanation.walkthrough: 'shortened' drops the last letter of the frequently word before 'including' wraps it round the rest.

clue.text: Large mass removed from noiseless instrument

indicators.note: removed from tells us the mass letter goes out of the noiseless word, the large letter taking its place

parts.note: mute means noiseless

clue.text: Yule fowl cooked in a terrible way

indicators.note: cooked means the letters of Yule fowl are prepared in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A Christmas bird roasted very badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Woefully means deplorably or wretchedly, describing something done badly.

clue.text: What was written on valentine's borders, to ponder when rising

explanation.walkthrough: 'when rising' turns MULL upwards to LLUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Vellum is fine parchment, a material once used for writing documents.

clue.text: Supporters generally unpredictable, with following for Republican

parts.note: random means unpredictable

explanation.walkthrough: 'following for Republican' swaps R in RANDOM for F.
explanation.definitionFit: Fandom is the body of fans as a whole, supporters collectively.

clue.text: The King's residence to honour with presence and light

parts.note: to grace an event is to honour it by attending
to light on something is to land on it

explanation.surface: A royal residence honoured by a visit and filled with light.
explanation.walkthrough: The King is Elvis Presley, whose Memphis home was Graceland.

clue.text: Place bone in hollow

clue.text: Other people's time with next of kin?

parts.note: an heir is usually the nearest relative to inherit

clue.text: Did toy get soil-encrusted imp to come back?

encrusted means the soil word coats the imp word

parts.note: dirt is soil
an elf is a mischievous imp
